from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Intuition: What is Information?", [
            "Information is the reduction of uncertainty.",
            "Surprise drives how much we learn.",
            "Binary splits provide exactly one bit."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Visualize a single binary choice (Yes/No) turning into certainty. #FFFFFF
        uncertainty_circle = Circle(radius=0.8, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(uncertainty_circle, 'C3')
        q_mark = Text("?", font_size=48).move_to(uncertainty_circle.get_center())
        self.add(uncertainty_circle, q_mark)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # Animation: Yes/No decision splits it
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid['C2'], end=self.grid['C4'], color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(arrow))
        self.play(FadeOut(q_mark), FadeOut(uncertainty_circle))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Fade in a probability distribution changing from uniform to spike. #00FF00
        dist_bars = VGroup(*[Rectangle(height=1.0, width=0.5, color=GREY, fill_opacity=0.5).move_to(self.grid[f'E{i+1}']) for i in range(4)])
        self.add(dist_bars)
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Change to spike (high probability on one)
        spike = Rectangle(height=2.0, width=0.5, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=1.0).move_to(self.grid['E3'])
        self.play(Transform(dist_bars, spike))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the reduction in possible outcomes as information arrives. #FFFF00
        box_group = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.6, color=WHITE).move_to(self.grid[f'B{i+1}']) for i in range(1, 5)])
        self.add(box_group)
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Shrink boxes to 1
        self.play(FadeOut(box_group[0]), FadeOut(box_group[1]), FadeOut(box_group[3]))
        self.play(box_group[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00").scale(1.5))

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Quantifying Uncertainty: The Entropy Formula", 
            ["Entropy quantifies average surprise.", "High entropy means high uncertainty.", "Lower entropy means clearer paths."]
        )
        
        # Setup Math Elements
        formula = MathTex("H(X) = -\\sum P(x) \\log_2 P(x)", color=WHITE)
        formula.set_color_by_tex("\\log_2", "#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        bit = Text("0", color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(bit, 'D4')
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), FadeIn(bit))
        self.play(bit.animate.move_to(formula.get_center()), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(bit))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 1, 0.2], y_range=[0, 1, 0.2], axis_config={"color": WHITE})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: -x * np.log2(x + 1e-9) if x > 0 else 0, color="#FFA500")
        graph = VGroup(axes, curve)
        self.place_at_grid(graph, 'E3', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), Create(graph))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Strategy: Maximizing Information Gain", [
            "Wordle strategy maximizes information gain.",
            "Choose words that shrink pools.",
            "Information gain reduces the decision tree."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        root = Circle(radius=0.2, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        self.place_at_grid(root, 'A3')
        
        tree = VGroup(root)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # Draw a basic decision tree
        layer1 = [Circle(radius=0.15, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1) for _ in range(3)]
        for i, node in enumerate(layer1):
            self.place_at_grid(node, f'C{i+2}')
            line = Line(root.get_center(), node.get_center(), color="#00FF00")
            tree.add(line, node)
            
        self.play(Create(tree))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Highlight path
        highlight = Circle(radius=0.25, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0).move_to(tree[2].get_center())
        self.play(Create(highlight))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF0000")
        
        # Prune branches
        to_prune = VGroup(tree[3], tree[4])
        self.play(FadeOut(to_prune), FadeOut(tree[1]))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Feedback Loop: Iterative Optimization", [
            "Feedback updates our probability distribution.",
            "Each guess refines the target.",
            "Entropy drops with every new clue."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show an arrow cycle representing input-output-feedback. #FFFFFF (text), #00FFFF (arrows)
        loop_group = VGroup(
            Square(side_length=1.5, color=WHITE),
            Arrow(start=UP*1.2, end=DOWN*1.2, color="#00FFFF"),
            Arrow(start=LEFT*1.2, end=RIGHT*1.2, color="#00FFFF")
        )
        self.place_at_grid(loop_group, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(loop_group), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight the 'update' phase in the loop with bolding. #FFFF00
        # In this visual, we color a part of the loop yellow.
        self.play(loop_group[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Visualize the model accuracy line rising over iterations. #00FF00 (line)
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 1, 0.25], x_length=3, y_length=2).scale(0.7)
        graph = axes.plot(lambda x: 1 - (0.5)**x, color="#00FF00")
        accuracy_group = VGroup(axes, graph)
        self.place_at_grid(accuracy_group, "E4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(accuracy_group), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Cracking the Code: Information Theory and Entropy in Wordle
outline.target_audience: University students (CS or Data Science focus)

sections.title: The Intuition: What is Information?
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'surprise' as the core of information. Using binary trees, explain that information is the reduction of uncertainty. Prerequisite: Basic probability (P(x)).
sections.example: A 'Robot Detective' trying to find a cat hidden in one of 4 boxes. Each 'yes/no' question splits the search space in half, providing exactly 1 bit of information.

sections.title: Quantifying Uncertainty: The Entropy Formula
sections.content: Define Entropy (H) as the weighted average of information (surprises). Present the formula H(X) = -Σ P(x) log2 P(x) using a visual bar chart where the height represents probability and the width represents the 'surprise' value.
sections.example: Visualizing Wordle guess outcomes: A uniform distribution of outcomes (many possible words left) results in high entropy, while a skewed distribution (only 1-2 words left) results in low entropy.

sections.title: The Strategy: Maximizing Information Gain
sections.content: Explain that an optimal Wordle bot chooses a word that produces the most 'Expected Information Gain' (the greatest reduction in entropy). Show a transition animation where a 'bad' word shrinks the pool by 10% vs a 'good' word shrinking it by 90%.
sections.example: Comparing 'XYLID' (rare letters, low entropy) vs 'ARISE' (common letters, high entropy) against a pool of 2,300 words. 'ARISE' provides a much larger partition of the probability space.

sections.title: The Feedback Loop: Iterative Optimization
sections.content: Summarize the process: Guess -> Observe Pattern (Green/Yellow/Gray) -> Update Probability Distribution -> Repeat. Emphasize that entropy is dynamic—it decreases with every piece of feedback.
sections.example: A 'Cyber-Squirrel' algorithm: It narrows down a target word from 2,000 choices to 1 within 3-4 moves by prioritizing 'Maximum Entropy' guesses to prune the decision tree.
